top_story.headline: A discharge petition on immigration relief sits one signature short of 218
top_story.dek: Discharge Petition No. 25 stands at 217 of 218 signatures while the House holds no votes.
paragraphs: Discharge Petition No. 25, which would bring H.R. 1589 to the House floor, has 217 of the 218 signatures it needs, one to go. The petition seeks consideration of the bill to authorize the cancellation of removal and adjustment of status of certain aliens, and for other purposes. The petition is tied to H.Res. 1414, sponsored by Sylvia R. Garcia.

No open discharge petition gained signers, was filed, or reached 218 since October 13, 2026. A second petition, No. 27, is two signatures short at 216 of 218. It seeks consideration of H.R. 185 to advance responsible policies (H.Res. 1430, sponsor Thomas Massie).
The House met on Thursday, October 15, from 10 a.m. to 11:04 a.m. and held no recorded votes. Its next scheduled meeting is a pro forma session at 10 a.m. on Monday, October 19.
No new Congressional Record issue has been published since this one (first covered 2026-10-16); the summary below is carried over.

sections.headline: A short House session, a Senate pro forma, and 35 new measures
paragraphs: The Senate met in pro forma session at 9:30:01 a.m. on Thursday, October 15, 2026, and adjourned 26 seconds later at 9:30:27 a.m. until 9 a.m. on Monday, October 19. No Senate committee meetings were held.

The House met at 10 a.m. and adjourned at 11:04 a.m., with Representative Wittman serving as Speaker pro tempore. There were no Yea and Nay votes, no recorded votes and no quorum calls, and no committee reports were filed. Members introduced 30 bills, 1 joint resolution and 4 resolutions. Among the more newsworthy: two campaign-finance bills (H.R. 10814 and H.R. 10825), a Russia energy sanctions bill (H.R. 10828) and a bill on Wall Street records related to Jeffrey Epstein (H.R. 10820). Every measure follows.

items: H.R. 10810, sponsored by Rep. Nanette Barragán (D-CA-44) — would establish a National Patient Safety Board; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and, in addition, the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.

H.R. 10811, sponsored by Rep. Everton Blair (D-GA-13) — would raise the allowable government share of a fixed guideway capital investment grant project when the recipient protects small business owners from project-related transportation interruptions; referred to the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

H.R. 10812, sponsored by Rep. Mike Carey (R-OH-15) — the Armenian American Cultural Heritage Act, which would recognize Library of Congress collections related to Armenian Americans and celebrate Armenian American heritage; referred to the House Committee on House Administration.

H.R. 10813, sponsored by Rep. Mike Carey (R-OH-15) — the Historic Preservation and Land Conservation Certainty Act, which would provide an election to resolve certain open partnership controversies involving donations of conservation easements; referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10814, sponsored by Rep. Yvette Clarke (D-NY-9) — would amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to require political ads to carry a statement when generative AI was used to create any image or video footage; referred to the House Committee on House Administration.

H.R. 10815, sponsored by Rep. J. Correa (D-CA-46) — the Bright Beginnings Act, which would create a tax credit for amounts child care providers pay to advance innovation and access for developmentally disabled individuals; referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10816, sponsored by Rep. Debbie Dingell (D-MI-6) — the DORIE Act of 2026, which would prohibit naming Department of Defense assets for sitting Presidents; referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10817, sponsored by Rep. Debbie Dingell (D-MI-6) — the U.S.S. Doris Miller Act of 2026, which would express the sense of Congress on naming a naval aircraft carrier for Mess Attendant Third Class Doris "Dorie" Miller; referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10818, sponsored by Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-1) — the Fire Service Workforce Stability Act of 2026, which would exclude certain income of firefighters and emergency medical services personnel from gross income; referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
H.R. 10819, sponsored by Rep. James Gallagher (R-CA-1) — would establish a United States-India Interparliamentary Group; referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.

H.R. 10820, sponsored by Rep. Robert Garcia (D-CA-42) — the Epstein Wall Street Records Act of 2026, which would require disclosure of supervisory records of certain financial institutions that relate to Jeffrey Epstein; referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.

H.R. 10821, sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) — would amend the Federal Deposit Insurance Act to change the Standard Maximum Deposit Insurance Amount; referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.

H.R. 10822, sponsored by Rep. Pat Harrigan (R-NC-10) — would restrict governmental use of automated license plate reader systems; referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and, in addition, the House Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10823, sponsored by Rep. Val Hoyle (D-OR-4) — the Northwest Wetlands Voluntary Incentives Program Act, which would authorize the Secretary of the Interior to set up a regional pilot program to improve habitat and water availability for shorebirds, waterfowl and other wetlands-dependent birds; referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.

H.R. 10824, sponsored by Rep. George Latimer (D-NY-16) — the Stroke Education and EMS Care Improvement Act of 2026, which would direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to create a standardized stroke education program for emergency medical services clinicians; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10825, sponsored by Rep. Michael Lawler (R-NY-17) — would prohibit Joint Fundraising Committees that include federal candidates and Independent Expenditure-Only Political Committees from making disbursements on paid media; referred to the House Committee on House Administration.

H.R. 10826, sponsored by Rep. Teresa Leger Fernandez (D-NM-3) — the Justice for Citizens Wrongfully Detained by ICE Act, which would create a private right of action for U.S. citizens arrested or detained by immigration officers or law enforcement officers enforcing immigration laws without a warrant or probable cause; referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10827, sponsored by Rep. Ryan Mackenzie (R-PA-7) — the Protection of Syrian Religious and Ethnic Minorities Act, which would require the Secretary of State to report on senior Syrian officials alleged to have facilitated certain human rights abuses; referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs and, in addition, the House Committees on the Judiciary and Financial Services.

H.R. 10828, sponsored by Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-NY-5) — would impose sanctions with respect to oil and gas extraction and refinement by the Russian Federation; referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs and, in addition, the House Committees on the Judiciary, Financial Services, Ways and Means, Oversight and Government Reform, and Rules.

H.R. 10829, sponsored by Rep. Marie Perez (D-WA-3) — would direct the Elder Justice Coordinator of the Federal Trade Commission to establish a website and hotline for victims of fraud and scams aimed at elders; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10830, sponsored by Rep. Jefferson Shreve (R-IN-6) — would direct the Comptroller General of the United States to study the development and adoption of pattern books in the United States; referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.

H.R. 10831, sponsored by Rep. David Taylor (R-OH-2) — would amend the Mineral Leasing Act for Acquired Lands and the Mineral Leasing Act to increase the State share of oil and gas leasing revenue from acquired lands; referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.

H.R. 10832, sponsored by Rep. Claudia Tenney (R-NY-24) — would amend the Iran Threat Reduction and Syria Human Rights Act of 2012 to improve coordination of efforts to promote internet freedom and access to information in Iran; referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs and, in addition, the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
H.R. 10833, sponsored by Rep. Shri Thanedar (D-MI-13) — would allow the Secretary to insure mortgages for certain first-time homebuyers; referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.

H.R. 10834, sponsored by Rep. Dina Titus (D-NV-1) — would require the Administrator of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to start a process to reevaluate corporate average fuel economy standards; referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10835, sponsored by Rep. Norma Torres (D-CA-35) — would amend the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to set up demonstration and pilot projects for education and training programs in advanced manufacturing; referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

H.R. 10836, sponsored by Rep. Eugene Vindman (D-VA-7) — would amend the Uniform Code of Military Justice to prohibit the live broadcast of military executions; referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10837, sponsored by Rep. Eugene Vindman (D-VA-7) — would bar people convicted of bribery, ethics violations or violations of the Foreign Agents Registration Act from serving in the executive branch; referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
H.R. 10838, sponsored by Rep. Eugene Vindman (D-VA-7) — would extend the statute of limitations for making false statements to Congress; referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10839, sponsored by Rep. James Walkinshaw (D-VA-11) — would reduce the heat island effect and associated ground-level ozone pollution from Federal facilities; referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

H.J. Res. 219, sponsored by Rep. Scott Perry (R-PA-10) — proposes a constitutional amendment requiring a Judge to be a natural born citizen of the United States; referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

H. Res. 1625, sponsored by Rep. Suzanne Bonamici (D-OR-1) — expresses support for a whole child approach to education and recognizes the role of parents, educators and community members in it; referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

H. Res. 1626, sponsored by Rep. John Moolenaar (R-MI-2) — supports designating the week of October 18 through 24, 2026, as "National Chemistry Week"; referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.

H. Res. 1627, sponsored by Rep. Delia Ramirez (D-IL-3) — reaffirms the commitment of the House of Representatives to preserve and expand pathways to citizenship; referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

H. Res. 1628, sponsored by Rep. Mike Thompson (D-CA-4) — supports designating the week beginning October 10, 2026, as "National Wildlife Refuge Week"; referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
